note: a new sentence in 1738 (capital *Sed* after its full stop at 20:21) and a new paragraph, as the BSB; 20:23 explains it (*enim*), its question and answer reported (*an … dēbērent*, *ut … aggrederentur*) (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Itaque adorti sunt Israelitae Benjamitas die secundo:
note: a new paragraph, the second day (BSB) (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Tum omnes Israelitarum copiae Bethel petiverunt, et illic plorantes ante Jovam manserunt, et eo die ad vesperum jejunarunt, eique solida sacrificia et pro salute fecerunt,
note: a new paragraph (BSB); *eīque* in lower case: the draft's capital came from a line break in Wikisource, mid-sentence (1738 *eique*; pronouns for God are lower case, settled *eīque* 117); 20:28's question and answer reported (*rūrsumne … dēbērent*, *ut īrent: nam … sēsē … datūrum*) (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Tum Israelitae insidiis circa Gabaam collocatis,
note: a new paragraph, the third day (BSB) (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: adversum quos egressi Benjamitae, extra oppidum pellecti sunt. Quum enim in semitis, quarum altera fert Bethel, altera Gabaam, principio circiter triginta Israelitas, sicut superioribus proeliis, illi victores occidissent,
note: lower case after 20:30's colon (Castellio's period goes on: *ōrdinārunt: adversum quōs …*), as the settled narrative books after a colon; the Benjamites' thought (20:32 *putābant eōs victōs cēdere*) and the Israelites' plan (*ut … pertraherent*) are reported, unquoted though the BSB quotes them (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: omnes ex loco suo consurrexerunt, et aciem apud Baalthamar instaurarunt, simulque Israelitarum insidiae in Gabaanis pratis positae ingruere coeperunt,
note: *et* and *simulque* in lower case: mid-sentence capitals from Wikisource's line breaks (1738's own capital *Et* after a comma is the printer's; its *simulque* is lower case) (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: et a parte Gabaae venerunt decem hominum millia ex omnibus Israelitis delecta: atque ita commisso atroci proelio
note: *atque* in lower case after the colon, mid-sentence (1738 *atque*; the draft's capital from a Wikisource line break) (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Jova Benjamitas ingruentis sibi mali ignaros Israelitis fudit, qui ex illis eo die viginti quinque millia et centum arma ferentium hominum corruperunt.
note: *quī* (relative) in lower case after the comma (1738 *qui*; the capital from a Wikisource line break) (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Benjamitis enim, quum ab eis superari viderentur, locum dederant, freti insidiis, quas contra Gabaam collocaverant,
note: a new paragraph at the BSB's break (its 20:36b, which is Castellio's whole 20:36: the explanation of the ambush); a comma closing the *cum* clause before its main verb (1738 has it), *frētī* in lower case (a Wikisource line-break capital; 1738 *freti* after a semicolon) and a comma before the relative *quās* (1738) (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Fuerat autem Israelitis statutum cum insidiis tempus, ut tum gladiis rem gererent, quum illi fumum ex oppido evectum ostendissent.
note: a new paragraph, the signal agreed (BSB); the verse ends with 1738's full stop (*ostendissent.* then *Igitur*), not Wikisource's comma (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Igitur quum ab oppido coepisset fumus columnae in modum efferri, et Israelitae proelium instaurarent, Benjamitae (qui initio circiter triginta Israelitarum occiderant, rati eos cedere, sicuti superioribus proeliis fecerant)
note: a new sentence, as 1738 (full stop at 20:38, capital *Igitur*): the proposal's lower case followed Wikisource's comma; the parenthesis kept as the draft (1738 prints only the closing one); the Benjamites' thought reported (*ratī eōs cēdere*) (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: terga verterunt Israelitis, silvamque petierunt: in qua proelio excepti ab illis perdebantur, qui ex oppidis aderant.
note: *in quā* in lower case after the colon (1738 *in qua*; the capital from a Wikisource line break) (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Ita circumventi Benjamitae, et in fuga facile protriti sunt, donec ventum est contra Gabaam ab ortu solis,
note: *dōnec* in lower case, mid-sentence (1738 *donec*; a Wikisource line-break capital) (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Inde in silvam versi, fugerunt ad rupem Remmonis, caesis passim per semitas quinque eorum millibus, et praeterea instante a tergo hoste usque ad Gedeomum, duobus millibus.
note: a new paragraph, the flight to Rimmon (BSB); *et prætereā* in lower case, mid-sentence (the capital from a Wikisource line break, and 1738's *Et* after a comma the printer's) (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Summa Benjamitarum arma ferentium militum, qui eo die ceciderunt, fuit viginti quinque millia.
note: a new paragraph, the sum of the dead and the end of the war (BSB) (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Igitur Bethel profecti, ibi apud Deum ad vesperum manserunt, et multo cum fletu apud Israelitarum Deum Jovam questi sunt,

text: Postero die mane, constructo illic altari, solida Jovae sacrificia proque salute fecerunt:
note: proofread: 1738's colon at the verse's end (*fecerunt: | ac si qui*), not a new full stop inside the period; otherwise as decided (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: ac si qui ex ulla Israeliticarum tribuum ad conventus ad Jovam non adfuissent, quaesiverunt. Intercesserat enim gravissimum sacramentum, quo in eos capitis poena sanciebatur, qui ad Jovam apud Maspham non adfuissent.
note: proofread: lower case *ac* after 21:4's colon, as 1738 (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Quum igitur eos Benjamitarum consanguineorum suorum poeniteret, et dolerent unam tunc ex Israelitis abscissam esse tribum,
note: a new paragraph (BSB, and 1738); the grief and the question (21:6–8) are reported (*dolērent ūnam … abscissam esse*, *quō pactō … prōspicerent*, *ecquī … nōn adfuissent*), unquoted (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Quod quum lustrato exercitu compertum esset, mittit eo civitas duodecim militum millia, cum praecepto, ut Jabenses Galaaditas adorti, etiam mulieres et parvulos ferro trucident,
note: a new paragraph, the expedition (BSB); the command (21:10–11) is reported (*cum præceptō, ut … trucīdent … ēvertant*), unquoted (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Inventae sunt autem ex Jabensibus quadringentae puellae virgines, et a virorum concubitu intactae, quas illi in castra apud Siluntem in Chananaea sita adduxerunt.
note: a new paragraph (BSB) (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Tum civitas omnis misit ad Benjamitas, qui in rupe Remmonis erant, qui cum illis colloquerentur eisque pacem offerrent:
note: proofread: 1738's colon at the verse's end (*offerrent: | reuocatisque*), not a new full stop inside the period; otherwise as decided (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: revocatisque tum Benjamitis, nuptum dederunt conservatas ex Jabensibus mulieres.
note: proofread: lower case *revocātīsque* after 21:13's colon, as 1738 (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Sed quum hae pauciores illis essent, et populus Benjamitarum vicem doleret, mutilatis a Jova tribubus Israelitarum,
note: a new paragraph (BSB); the elders' question (21:16–18) is indirect (*quānam ratiōne … possent*), unquoted (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: et eorum Benjamitarum, qui evaserant, futura esset hereditas, ne tribus Israelitica deleretur,
note: *nē* in lower case, mid-sentence (1738 *ne*; the capital from a Wikisource line break) (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Igitur quum comperirent festum Jovae quotannis agi Silunte a septentrione Bethelis, ab oriente semitae, quae a Bethele fert Sichemam, et a meridie Lebnae,
note: a new paragraph, the plan at Shiloh (BSB); *Jōvæ* with only its capital (the draft's *JOvae* is a typing slip: 1738 *Iouæ*) (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Benjamitis in hunc modum praeceperunt: “Ite, et vos per vineas in insidiis collocate.

text: Quod si illarum parentes aut fratres ad nos expostulatum venerint, rogabimus ut nobis factum condonent vestrum, qui non tot mulieres in bello ceperimus, ut sua cuique daretur: illos quidem eas vobis non dedisse, ut culpam commisisse videantur.”
note: *quī* (the relative of cause, *quī nōn … cēperīmus*) in lower case after the comma (1738 *qui*; a Wikisource line-break capital); the elders' speech closes (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Atque ita fecerunt Benjamitae: raptasque de saltantibus totidem, quot erant ipsi, mulieres abegerunt, et in suum patrimonium regressi, oppida instaurarunt atque incoluerunt.
note: a new paragraph after the speech (BSB) (Claude, 2026-11-19)

text: Per ea tempora, quum nullus Israelitarum rex esset, suo quisque vivebat arbitratu.
note: a new paragraph, the book's closing refrain (BSB) (Claude, 2026-11-19)
